about: English draft for the 50 stages and 7 planets (names, hints, story lines). Content only: the file format waits for the architect's i18n design and will be converted then. Story = the triplets' view, separate from the hint. Keys follow the Korean source in prototypes/seven-steps/src/levels.js and design/levels/chapters.json (matched by n and Korean name).

glossary.선돌 / 석상 (KEEP으로 남은 몸): standing stone (in hints: 'stone'). One word for both Korean terms so players learn one thing
glossary.형제, 세쌍둥이: brother, the triplets (first / second / third brother; teal, ochre, russet scarf = identity only)
glossary.숫자 문: numbered gate (opens only on that step)
glossary.석상 수 문: count gate (opens when exactly that many stones stand)
glossary.구멍·구덩이: hole (you can see the stars through it)
glossary.N번째 걸음: the Nth step (always spelled out: 'the 7th step')

chapters.concept: Home: broken pillars and a small moss-covered observatory ruin
chapters.intro: At the very edge of the sky map, someone drew a ring of stones. The three leave home.

chapters.concept: A moon full of holes with stars showing through
chapters.intro: Stars show through the ground here. Where the path breaks, a brother becomes the path.

chapters.concept: A planet of counting, numbers carved into every pillar
chapters.intro: The old watchers carved numbers into the stones: which step lets you through.

chapters.concept: A frozen moon, wooden rails and frosted stone
chapters.intro: A frozen moon. Once you slide, you do not stop until something stops you.

chapters.concept: Walls that move on wooden joints and brass levers
chapters.intro: A world of timber and brass. The seventh step turns the machinery.

chapters.concept: Cracked floors and gates that count the standing stones
chapters.intro: The floor cracks under every footstep. The gates count the stones left standing.

chapters.concept: The last planet: a ring of standing stones beyond a mossy bog
chapters.intro: The end of the map. Beyond the bog, standing stones form a circle.

stages.name: Seven Steps
stages.hint: Exactly 7 steps at a time. The exit only opens on the 7th.
stages.story: Count from the first step. On the seventh, the sky lines up.

stages.name: Arrive Late
stages.hint: The exit is close. Stepping on it early does nothing. Wander, and arrive on the 7th.
stages.story: The door is right there, but not all the stars are out yet.

stages.name: Just the Right Path
stages.hint: Only one path to the exit is exactly 7 steps long.
stages.story: Many forks, but only one path is seven steps long.

stages.name: Turned to Stone
stages.hint: After 7 steps, you choose. KEEP: leave a standing stone here. A stone keeps a plate pressed.
stages.story: The eldest stops. Right there he turns to stone and holds the door.

stages.name: The Near Plate
stages.hint: Two plates. Which one can you stand on with your 7th step?
stages.story: The near plate is an even count away. Seven never lands there.

stages.name: The Stone in the Way
stages.hint: A stone opens the door, but it also blocks the spot it stands on.
stages.story: The brother who opened the door now stands in the shortcut.

stages.name: Two Doors
stages.hint: You can leave as many stones as you like, while brothers last.
stages.story: Two keep the doors. The third leaves home.

stages.name: A New Start
stages.hint: SWITCH: leave no stone. Instead, this spot becomes the next brother's start.
stages.story: Leave nothing behind. Hand your spot to your brother.

stages.name: Pass It On
stages.hint: No one gets there alone. Hand your 7th-step spot to the next brother.
stages.story: Too far for one. The three walk it together.

stages.name: A Bridge of Brothers
stages.hint: Step into a hole on your 7th step and the fallen brother becomes a bridge.
stages.story: Stars below the hole. Fall on the seventh step and you land as a bridge.

stages.name: Bridge or Stone
stages.hint: One brother for the bridge, one for the plate. Who goes where?
stages.story: One becomes a bridge, one becomes a stone.

stages.name: Waking on the Far Side
stages.hint: The brother who crossed the bridge hands over from there.
stages.story: The second crosses the bridge and hands over on the far side.

stages.name: Two Holes, Three Brothers
stages.hint: Two holes. Two bridges.
stages.story: Two holes means two bridges.

stages.name: Where We Started
stages.hint: Move the start far away, and the way back gets longer too.
stages.story: They passed the start far ahead. Now one has to come back.

stages.name: Numbered Gate
stages.hint: A numbered gate lets you through only on that step.
stages.story: The carved number says which step may pass.

stages.name: Plate Past the Gate
stages.hint: Pass the numbered gate, then stand on the plate.
stages.story: Beyond the numbered gate lies a plate.

stages.name: Numbers at the Fork
stages.hint: Numbered gates are not shortcuts. Count which step gets you there.
stages.story: The gates close the shortcuts. Count the long way round.

stages.name: Count Again from One
stages.hint: From a new start, counting begins again at 1.
stages.story: Too far for the first brother. The second starts again from one.

stages.name: Numbers and a Hole
stages.hint: Steps across the bridge count too.
stages.story: Crossing the bridge counts as steps.

stages.name: Two Numbers
stages.hint: Two numbered gates. Which step of the second brother?
stages.story: Where you hand over decides the second brother's numbers.

stages.name: The Carvers' Sum
stages.hint: One stone, one handover, one gate. Count every brother's steps.
stages.story: The last sum of the carved world: every brother's steps add up.

stages.name: A Slippery First Step
stages.hint: However far you slide on ice, it is one step.
stages.story: On ice, any slide is just one step.

stages.name: The Odd Curse
stages.hint: 7 is odd. Some squares can never be reached on foot alone. A slide on ice is 1 step, however far.
stages.story: On plain ground it never comes to seven. Seven is odd.

stages.name: Numbers on Ice
stages.hint: One slide is one step. Which step for the gate?
stages.story: One slide, one number.

stages.name: The Stone That Stops
stages.hint: Ice stops only at a wall. A stone is a wall.
stages.story: No wall? Then a brother becomes the wall.

stages.name: A Brother in the Slide
stages.hint: A stone stops a slide, but it blocks the path too. Where should it stand?
stages.story: Stand as the stopper, but not in the next brother's way.

stages.name: Hole at the End of the Ice
stages.hint: What if you slide into the hole on your 7th step?
stages.story: Sliding into the hole. If that is the seventh step...

stages.name: Frost Pass
stages.hint: The plate and the door are both beyond the ice.
stages.story: The edge of the frost moon. Plate and door wait past the ice.

stages.name: Lowering the Wall
stages.hint: Step on the lever with your 7th step and the wall goes down. Unlike a plate, one pull is enough.
stages.story: Step on the lever with the seventh step and the wall sinks.

stages.name: Open One, Close One
stages.hint: The lever flips every wall. An open way can close.
stages.story: One way opens, another way shuts.

stages.name: Raise It to Stop
stages.hint: The lever flips every wall. A lowered wall rises and stops the ice.
stages.story: Raise the sunken wall to stop the slide.

stages.name: Lever and Plate
stages.hint: A lever once, a plate always. You need both.
stages.story: A lever needs one pull. A plate needs someone standing.

stages.name: Lever and Numbers
stages.hint: Once the wall is down, count the new way to the gates.
stages.story: When the walls change, so does the count to the gate.

stages.name: Lever and Handover
stages.hint: The brother who pulled the lever: where does the next one start?
stages.story: The one who pulled the lever hands over.

stages.name: The Joinery Machine
stages.hint: Lever, ice, stone, handover. Get off the joinery world.
stages.story: The way off this world is a machine: lever, ice and brothers.

stages.name: Floor That Holds Once
stages.hint: Cracked floor breaks once you walk over it. Stop on it with your 7th step and it becomes a bridge forever.
stages.story: The floor behind you crumbles. Stop on it, and it sets.

stages.name: Holes in a Crumbling Road
stages.hint: Floor you cross falls in. Leave yourself a way back.
stages.story: Choose which road to break and which to keep.

stages.name: Leave Only One
stages.hint: The number on the gate is the number of standing stones. It opens only at exactly that many.
stages.story: The gate counts the stones. Just one.

stages.name: The Brother Who Is the Key
stages.hint: Where do you get a stone to open the gate?
stages.story: In a dead end nobody visits, a brother stands as the key.

stages.name: Pass Before You Stay
stages.hint: A gate marked 0 closes as soon as any stone stands.
stages.story: A gate marked zero. Get through before anyone turns to stone.

stages.name: Not a Stone
stages.hint: Sealed floor becomes a path, but it does not count as a stone.
stages.story: Sealed floor is a path, not a stone.

stages.name: Crumbling Sums
stages.hint: Neither bridges nor sealed floor are stones. How many is the gate waiting for?
stages.story: Bridges and sealed floor are not stones. The gate stays shut to the end.

stages.name: Two Steps a Square
stages.hint: Mud takes two steps per square.
stages.story: Bog mud: two steps for one square.

stages.name: Mud and Numbers
stages.hint: Through the mud, you skip a number.
stages.story: Step in the mud and a number goes by.

stages.name: Ice and Mud
stages.hint: Ice: many squares, one step. Mud: one square, two steps.
stages.story: Ice is quick. Mud is slow.

stages.name: Seven by Seven Room
stages.hint: Bridge, plate, numbered gate, lever. Three brothers.
stages.story: Bridge, plate, number and lever, and only three brothers.

stages.name: Lever and the Count
stages.hint: If the brother who pulled the lever stays as a stone, the 0 gate closes.
stages.story: If the one who pulled the lever stays, the zero gate shuts.

stages.name: Brothers Become the Road
stages.hint: Both brothers become the road.
stages.story: Two brothers become the road. The third walks it.

stages.name: Seven Sevens
stages.hint: Seven squares by seven squares. Count them all.
stages.story: Seven rows of seven. The altar is near.

stages.name: The Stone Circle
stages.hint: When two brothers stand as stones, the altar opens.
stages.story: Two brothers stand in the circle. The third's seventh step reaches the altar.

stars.3: In one go (no undo, no restart)
stars.constellation: Each planet's seven stages are the seven stars of the Big Dipper. Stage 50 is the North Star.

notes: 46 '칠칠의 방' plays on 칠칠 (seven-seven, 7x7) and its sound in everyday Korean; 'Seven by Seven Room' keeps the counting, the wordplay has no English match.
23 'The Odd Curse' keeps the parity joke (odd = 홀수).
Stage 50 and chapter 7 share the name 'The Stone Circle' as in Korean (원형 제단).
